title: Remove legacy osbuild_component vars; component-file package tracker with submenu

questions.prompt: Which variables and data should be removed?
questions.description: Legacy pair: osbuild_components (name list) + osbuild_component_defs (inline catalog in roles/osbuild/defaults/main.yml). The catalog is built from vars/packages/<Distro>.yml via system_packages/system_groups. Consumers: validate_components.yml, osbuild_component_sources in tasks/main.yml, blueprint.toml.j2, build.sh.j2, files/bootc/build.yml ('nvidia' in osbuild_components).
questions.recommendedAnswer: Remove osbuild_components, osbuild_component_defs, validate_components.yml, osbuild_component_sources and the vars/packages taxonomy load. osbuild_blueprint_components + component files become the only package source.

options.label: osbuild_components (list) in defaults and all 12 playbooks + osbuild.yml
osbuild_component_defs catalog in defaults/main.yml
tasks/validate_components.yml
osbuild_component_sources fact in tasks/main.yml
vars/packages/{Fedora,AlmaLinux,Rocky}.yml + 'Load package taxonomy' task + roles/osbuild/vars/packages.yml

questions.prompt: Should osbuild_blueprint_components keep its name, or be renamed to osbuild_components after the legacy var is gone?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Keep osbuild_blueprint_components. A rename reuses a name with a different meaning, so old playbooks would fail in confusing ways instead of plainly.

options.label: Keep osbuild_blueprint_components
Rename to osbuild_components

questions.prompt: What happens to blueprint.toml.j2 (osbuild_use_blueprint_template mode)? Every playbook sets it to false.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Delete blueprint.toml.j2, osbuild_use_blueprint_template and osbuild_blueprint_template. Builds use either a static blueprint or component composition.

options.label: Delete template mode
Port it to read component files
Leave it (broken) and mark deprecated

questions.prompt: The bootc path (tasks/bootc.yml -> build.sh.j2, files/bootc/build.yml) reads osbuild_component_defs, including flatpaks, bootc_repos, copr_repos and blueprint_only. How should it change?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Port build.sh.j2 to the loaded component files (_osbuild_bp_components). Add optional fields flatpaks, bootc_repos and copr_repos to the component file schema, and replace 'nvidia' in osbuild_components with 'nvidia' in osbuild_blueprint_components.

options.label: Port bootc to component files (extend schema with optional fields)
Remove the bootc path entirely
Out of scope: keep a minimal bootc-only var, follow up later

questions.prompt: Static-blueprint playbooks (osbuild-rocky-iso*, almalinux-iso*, rocky-cuda-container, osbuild.yml) set osbuild_components only for validation, sources and the nvidia check. What should happen to them?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Delete the osbuild_components block from them and keep them working on their static blueprint. Repos they need move to osbuild_extra_repo_urls or are already in the static TOML. No new component files for AlmaLinux in this goal.

options.label: Delete the var; keep the static blueprints
Convert them to component composition (create almalinux/10 component files)
Delete playbooks superseded by *-components.yml variants

questions.prompt: Which tracker capabilities must work against component files?
questions.description: Component files live at roles/osbuild/files/<distro>/<major>/<arch>/components/<name>.yml. Today only rocky/10/x86_64 exists. Edits must preserve comments and key order (ruamel.yaml round-trip).
questions.recommendedAnswer: list, search, add, remove, verify (repo lookup before add) and the TUI. The 'build' manifest export is dropped, because the playbook's osbuild_blueprint_components list is now the build selection.

options.label: list: components and package counts per distro/major/arch
search: find which component(s) contain a package
add: add package(s) to a component file
remove: remove package(s) from a component file
verify: check the package exists in repos before adding
create a new component file (label + packages)
keep 'build' manifest export (rewritten for components)
interactive TUI

questions.prompt: How does the tracker choose which component directory to operate on?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Discover every files/<distro>/<major>/<arch>/components directory. CLI uses --target rocky/10/x86_64, which defaults to the only one when there is a single directory. The TUI asks first only when more than one exists.

options.label: Discover dirs; --target flag; TUI prompts only if >1
Separate --distro/--major/--arch flags
Hard-code rocky/10/x86_64

questions.prompt: What should the component submenu do?
questions.description: Flow: main menu -> pick component -> package submenu.
questions.recommendedAnswer: In the submenu: a checkbox list of the component's packages, all pre-checked. Unchecking removes, after confirmation. Actions in the submenu: add packages (with optional repo verify), remove selected, show details (label, repo_urls, services), back.

options.label: Checkbox of packages (pre-checked); unchecked ones removed after confirm
Add packages from inside the submenu
Show component details (label, repo_urls, services, fragment)
Move selected packages to another component
Back to component list / main menu

questions.prompt: How should '@group' entries (comps groups) in packages lists be handled?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Treat them as ordinary entries that can be listed, added and removed. Skip repo verification for names starting with @.

options.label: Plain entries; skip verify for @ names
Show them in a separate section of the submenu

questions.prompt: When adding a package that already exists in another component of the same target, what should happen?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Warn and name the other component, then ask in the TUI or require --force in the CLI. Adding a duplicate within the same component is a no-op.

options.label: Warn + confirm/--force
Refuse
Allow silently

Run ansible-playbook --syntax-check on all playbooks, plus a generate-only run of osbuild-rocky-iso-components.yml whose blueprint package list matches the pre-change snapshot.

grep: no legacy var references left
